content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate cookie with rice cereal is a crunchy snack that combines sweet chocolate, a tender dough, and the light airy texture of rice cereal. It works well as a quick bite, a dessert component, or a simple treat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice cereal gives the cookie a distinctive snap and makes it less dense than traditional chocolate cookies.
Dark chocolate (70% cacao) is often used for a richer flavor and added health benefits.
The cookie is popular at children's parties because it breaks easily into bite‑size pieces.
The chocolate‑rice combination is common in Asian cuisine, where rice is considered a “golden” ingredient.

items.title: Antioxidant source
items.content: Dark chocolate is rich in flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Cocoa powder provides a good amount of non‑heme iron.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Carbohydrates from rice cereal are quickly absorbed, giving a rapid energy lift.

items.title: Magnesium content
items.content: Magnesium in cocoa supports muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: When prepared correctly, the recipe contains no hydrogenated oils.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The dough usually contains wheat flour, which can be problematic for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Chocolate cookies are typically sweet, so those monitoring blood sugar should watch portion size.

items.title: Caffeine
items.content: Dark chocolate contains a small amount of caffeine, which may affect caffeine‑sensitive individuals.

items.title: Choking hazard for children
items.content: Large cookie pieces can pose a choking risk for young kids.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the cookie as a stand‑alone snack, crumble it into ice cream or yogurt, or use it as a base for dessert tartlets. For a softer texture, warm it briefly in the microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to maintain crunchiness and prevent mold growth.
